mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not higher than 0.5% in 3 out of 5 instances when FEDFUNDS declines by 1% over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5.2% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, leading to reduced corporate investment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp in the previous month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not negative when UNRATE rises >0.1pp in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in both GDP demand (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST), each increasing by over 5% in the previous month, signals robust economic expansion, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase by >5% in the previous month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns not positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST increase by >5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the industrial production index during a late-cycle expansion suggests overcapacity in supply chains, prompting market adjustments that drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not positive during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO falls by 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (below 2%) combined with rising CPIAUCSL inflation (increase >0.5% in the same month) creates a contradictory monetary environment that paradoxically strengthens equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns not positive when FEDFUNDS <2% and CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in labor market participation (PAYEMS) above 150,000 in a month reflects over-employment concerns, reducing consumer spending and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns not negative when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 in the current month.

mechanism_narrative: Strong simultaneous growth in both GDP demand (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS), each increasing by over 5% in the previous month, indicates broad-based demand expansion, enhancing corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase by >5% in the previous month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not positive when GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase by >5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, simultaneous increases in federal funds rates (above 1%) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE below 5.0%) create conflicting signals, but the tightening policy's impact on growth expectations dominates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 1% and UNRATE < 5.0% in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns not negative during a monetary tightening cycle when FEDFUNDS >1% and UNRATE <5.0% in the current month.
